title: For the First Time, a Look at the Arctic Bobtail Squid in Its Natural Habitat
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyFor the First Time, a Look at the Arctic Bobtail Squid in Its Natural HabitatIt’s cold down there, but life finds a wayDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CDT on July 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThis mesmerizing deep sea creature is the Arctic bobtail squid (Rossia moelleri), and the photo you’re looking at—snapped by researchers using a remote camera—is the first image ever captured of it in its natural habitat.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoAs an extra bonus, egg clusters from the squid were also photographed, giving experts an unprecedented look at the life and reproduction of this cephalopod. The photo was captured in the Kong Oscar Fjord in Northeast Greenland National Park, and an account of the recording has been published in Polar Biology.A number of signals were used to identify the species, including its morphology and the placement of the eggs on a hard substrate—in this case, a sheltered fjord wall.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
